beats.subline: Friday, August 28, 2026 close — stocks slipped as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks tempered inflation optimism, though major indexes still closed out a positive week.
beats.body: Chip stocks led the pullback after new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh used his first Jackson Hole address to say this summer's cooler inflation readings don't yet show underlying improvement, tempering rate-cut bets; Nvidia and Intel weighed on the Nasdaq, but all three indexes still finished the week higher.

beats.headline: UK warns Israel against removing it from Gaza ceasefire coordination center
beats.body: The British government said any move by Israel to expel UK and other European officials from the US-backed Civil-Military Coordination Center in Gaza would 'undermine shared efforts,' after the Financial Times reported Israel was considering the expulsions; the warning comes as Trump's Gaza peace envoy Nikolay Mladenov continues to caution the ceasefire process risks a 'point of no return.'

beats.headline: Pentagon to pull bulk of ~200 troops from Nigeria as anti-ISIS mission winds down
beats.body: The Pentagon plans to withdraw most of the roughly 200 troops sent to northeastern Nigeria this year to fight Islamic State-linked militants, the New York Times reported, with officials crediting the deployment for counterterrorism gains including a May raid that killed senior ISIS figure Abu Bilal al-Minuki; a small team of trainers and intelligence analysts will stay behind.

beats.headline: Raytheon completes $50 million expansion of Mississippi radar and jammer plant
beats.body: RTX's Raytheon finished a 17,000-square-foot, $50 million expansion of its Forest, Mississippi facility that will produce Next Generation Jammer Mid-Band pods for the Navy and Australia along with other airborne radar systems, adding roughly 100 high-skill jobs by 2028.

beats.headline: Federal judge strikes down Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic as unlawful retaliation
beats.body: U.S. District Judge Rita Lin ruled the Defense Department violated Anthropic's First Amendment rights by branding it a supply-chain risk after the company refused to let Claude be used for mass surveillance or fully autonomous weapons, writing that 'the empty invocation of national security is not a blank check to punish and retaliate against government critics'; the administration is expected to appeal. Separately, Anthropic joined OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and 100-plus other firms in an open letter warning that AI-enabled cyberattacks will grow far more common in the coming months.

beats.headline: Both Bears starting cornerbacks banged up in physical joint practice with Titans
beats.body: Jaylon Johnson left Thursday's joint practice with the Titans early with an apparent right-arm injury and sat out the rest of the session, while fellow starter Tyrique Stevenson got hurt breaking up a red-zone pass but returned to work with the starters, leaving Chicago's secondary thin less than three weeks before the Sept. 13 opener at Carolina.
